# Omani crowd clothing
Two original dishdasha garments, kumma embroidery, mussar folds and furakha details fitted to the existing MIT Rocketbox Talker and Phone rigs. Base skin, faces and animation derive from PeopleModels/Animated; retain the parent pack's Microsoft MIT licence and sources.json. The new garment meshes and procedural textile textures are project-authored, released under the same MIT licence.

References (visual/cultural guidance only; no downloaded photographs used as textures):
- https://www.omanconsulate.com/en/tourism-in-oman.html
- https://experienceoman.om/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Marhaba-Oman_compressed.pdf

Generated by ../Source~/dress_omani.py in Blender 5.2. Existing five-person crowd count and behaviours retained. Clothing is bone-skinned; no cloth simulation, new lights or physics bodies.

October 26 model rebuild: 11 mm voxel union joins the garment, then the upper surface is fitted to the original anatomical shoulder/arm shape. Relaxed compression folds, unequal long folds, turned hems and cuff bands replace the boxy chest/cylindrical sleeves. The cloth has a 7,600-triangle target before opening/turning the hem. Source weights/UVs are transferred barycentrically and blended across new joins, normalized to four influences. Both faces/hands have refined topology; covered scalp and old shirt cuffs are removed, and the skin extends inside the collar with torso/neck weights. Separate floating neckline trim is removed. A cotton furakha follows the chest surface. Kumma has seated stitch geometry; mussar wraps follow its fitted volume.

Each FBX contains one near and one distance skinned mesh, sharing the original rig. Pair totals: 56,134 near / 16,839 distance triangles. Original feet, face identities, UVs and animation bindings remain. The material reuses InteriorModels/Shared_FabricCharcoal_Normal.jpg at restrained strength; its existing licence/attribution remain. Export uses FBX_SCALE_UNITS. Both levels, both clips and all five actors pass skin-bound/stretched-edge checks at nine phases in Unity; actual near/far silhouettes differ by no more than 0.22% in the fixed review.
